findings.issue_text: CalendarService.ts: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, so Prisma updateMany never bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; the call is a no-op that still issues a DB write per cache fetch
deleteCache.handler.ts: authorization only checks credential.userId === user.id, so team/org-owned credentials (teamId set, userId null) can never have their cache deleted by an admin
deleteCache.handler.ts: no check that the credential is a calendar credential, so any credential id owned by the user can have its calendarCache rows purged

CalendarService.ts: SelectedCalendar update runs even when the cache write throws or nothing was written, and stamps every calendar under the credential regardless of which were refreshed, making 'last updated' misleading

deleteCache.handler.ts: deleting CalendarCache rows does not stop the active Google watch channel or reset googleChannelId/syncToken on SelectedCalendar, so the next webhook push repopulates via incremental sync against an empty cache
deleteCache.handler.ts: UI keeps showing the cache dropdown until refetch because cacheUpdatedAt still comes from the stale response

connectedCalendars.handler.ts: new CalendarCacheRepository() bypasses the feature-flag-aware factory (CalendarCache.init/mock), so cache status is surfaced even when calendar cache is disabled and the mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is unreachable

CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx: deleteCacheMutation has no onSettled invalidation of connectedCalendars, so stale cacheUpdatedAt remains unless onSuccess/onChanged happens to refetch, which the onboarding path does not guarantee
CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx: timestamp is hard-coded to the 'en-US' locale, ignoring the user's locale and timezone despite useLocale() being available

getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts: updatedAt and googleChannelId added to UserWithCalendars type and UserRepository select but never read, causing other callers building UserWithCalendars to fail type-checking with no behavioral benefit
migration.sql: migration header comment claims the column was added without a default value, contradicting the actual statement which uses DEFAULT NOW()
test-gcal-webhooks.sh: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only syntax and fails on GNU sed (Linux/CI)
test-gcal-webhooks.sh: ENV_FILE='../.env' is relative to CWD rather than the script directory, so running from repo root writes to ../.env outside the repository
test-gcal-webhooks.sh: pgrep -f 'tmole 3000' also matches the script's own shell/grep invocations, causing a false 'already running' and an empty TUNNEL_URL from a stale or missing log
deleteCache.handler.ts: no tests for the new mutation (ownership rejection, team credential, successful delete) or for getCacheStatusByCredentialIds grouping
apps/web/package.json: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx as a devDependency, so the script depends on a runtime network fetch and an unpinned version

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, so Prisma updateMany never bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; the call is a no-op that still issues a DB write per cache fetch
matched_golden_ids: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that updateManyByCredentialId is invoked with an empty data object, causing Prisma updateMany to not update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (i.e., @updatedAt doesn’t bump). This is the same core issue as the golden comment about timestamps not updating and impacting cache tracking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts: authorization only checks credential.userId === user.id, so team/org-owned credentials (teamId set, userId null) can never have their cache deleted by an admin

adjudication.rationale: In deleteCache.handler.ts the credential lookup is `where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }`, so only credentials directly owned by the current user can pass. Any credential record that is not user-owned (e.g., delegated/team/org-owned where `userId` is null or different) will always fail with "Credential not found or access denied" and therefore its CalendarCache rows can never be deleted via this endpoint. The UI (CredentialActionsDropdown) does not gate the cache-deletion action on ownership/delegation—only on `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`—so it can expose a delete-cache action for such credentials that will then be unauthorized server-side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts: no check that the credential is a calendar credential, so any credential id owned by the user can have its calendarCache rows purged

adjudication.rationale: In deleteCache.handler.ts the mutation verifies the credential exists and is owned by the current user (where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }) before deleting from CalendarCache by credentialId. It does not validate the credential’s integration/type, so technically any user-owned credentialId can be passed. However, the only effect is deleting rows in the CalendarCache table for that credentialId; if non-calendar credentials never have CalendarCache rows (as suggested by the table’s purpose/usage), the deletion is a no-op. The finding’s claimed “problem” depends on an unstated requirement that only specific calendar credential types should be allowed, which is not verifiable from the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts: SelectedCalendar update runs even when the cache write throws or nothing was written, and stamps every calendar under the credential regardless of which were refreshed, making 'last updated' misleading

deleteCache.handler.ts: deleting CalendarCache rows does not stop the active Google watch channel or reset googleChannelId/syncToken on SelectedCalendar, so the next webhook push repopulates via incremental sync against an empty cache

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `deleteCache.handler.ts`, which only verifies credential ownership and then `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })`. Nothing in the diff shows that deleting cache is intended to also stop Google watch channels, nor does the diff show any dependency where an “active watch channel” or an “incremental sync” would break because `CalendarCache` rows are missing. The proposed finding references resetting `googleChannelId/syncToken` on `SelectedCalendar`, but this diff does not show any `syncToken` field or logic tying webhook handling to `CalendarCache` state. As a result, the claim about the next webhook repopulating via incremental sync against an empty cache is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts: UI keeps showing the cache dropdown until refetch because cacheUpdatedAt still comes from the stale response

adjudication.rationale: The server handler correctly deletes rows from `calendarCache`, and `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` will return `cacheUpdatedAt: null` after a subsequent fetch because the groupBy will no longer find rows for that credential. In the UI (`CredentialActionsDropdown`), the cache section is driven purely by the `cacheUpdatedAt` prop; the mutation does not locally clear it or invalidate/refetch `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` on its own, but it *does* call `onSuccess?.()`, and the parent passes `onSuccess={onChanged}`. Since the diff does not show what `onChanged` does, it’s not verifiable from this diff that the UI will fail to refetch and remain stale; the finding is speculative and also misattributes the issue to `deleteCache.handler.ts` rather than the client/query invalidation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts: new CalendarCacheRepository() bypasses the feature-flag-aware factory (CalendarCache.init/mock), so cache status is surfaced even when calendar cache is disabled and the mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is unreachable

adjudication.rationale: In connectedCalendars.handler.ts the new code directly imports and instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which always hits Prisma (`prisma.calendarCache.groupBy`). The diff also adds a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` that explicitly logs it should be used when “calendar-cache being disabled”, but the handler never uses the mock (nor an interface/factory), so any existing “disabled” path would be bypassed and cache status could still be queried/surfaced even when the feature is meant to be off.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx: deleteCacheMutation has no onSettled invalidation of connectedCalendars, so stale cacheUpdatedAt remains unless onSuccess/onChanged happens to refetch, which the onboarding path does not guarantee

adjudication.rationale: In CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx, deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback; unlike disconnectMutation, it does not invalidate/refetch any TRPC queries (e.g., viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars). Since cacheUpdatedAt is derived from the connectedCalendars query (enriched in connectedCalendars.handler.ts), deleting cache rows via deleteCache.handler.ts will not automatically update the cached query result, so the UI can remain stale unless the parent-provided onSuccess triggers a refetch/invalidation. The additional claim about the onboarding path not guaranteeing this is not directly verifiable from the diff, but the missing invalidation in the component is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts: updatedAt and googleChannelId added to UserWithCalendars type and UserRepository select but never read, causing other callers building UserWithCalendars to fail type-checking with no behavioral benefit

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `UserWithCalendars` being widened to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in the `Pick<SelectedCalendar,...>` element type, and the `UserRepository` Prisma `select` being updated to actually fetch those fields. There is nothing in the diff showing any other code constructing `UserWithCalendars` objects (e.g., object literals) that would now fail type-checking due to missing fields, nor any evidence the new fields are “never read.” The claim about type-check failures for other callers and “no behavioral benefit” is speculative and not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: migration.sql: migration header comment claims the column was added without a default value, contradicting the actual statement which uses DEFAULT NOW()

adjudication.rationale: In the new migration file, the autogenerated header comment under `Warnings:` says: "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value". However, the actual SQL executed is `ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();`, which *does* add the column with a default. This is a verifiable inconsistency in the diff (misleading migration metadata/comment), even though it doesn’t change runtime behavior of the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test-gcal-webhooks.sh: ENV_FILE='../.env' is relative to CWD rather than the script directory, so running from repo root writes to ../.env outside the repository

adjudication.rationale: In scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh the variable `ENV_FILE` is hard-coded as `"../.env"` and all reads/writes use that path directly (e.g., `if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then ...` and `sed ... "$ENV_FILE"`). This path is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script’s directory. If a developer runs the script from the repo root (a common case), `../.env` refers to the parent directory of the repo, so the script would create/modify an `.env` file outside the repository. There is no `cd` to the script directory or `ENV_FILE` derived from `$(dirname "$0")`, so the issue is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test-gcal-webhooks.sh: pgrep -f 'tmole 3000' also matches the script's own shell/grep invocations, causing a false 'already running' and an empty TUNNEL_URL from a stale or missing log

adjudication.rationale: The script uses `TMOLE_RUNNING=$(pgrep -f "tmole $TM_PORT")`. Because `pgrep -f` matches against the full command line, it can match the `pgrep` process itself since its argv contains the literal pattern string (`tmole 3000`). This can yield a non-empty `TMOLE_RUNNING` even when no `tmole` process is running, causing the script to take the “already running” branch and attempt to read `TUNNEL_URL` from `/tmp/tmole.log` (which may be missing/stale), leading to failure/incorrect behavior. This is a concrete defect in the added script logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts: no tests for the new mutation (ownership rejection, team credential, successful delete) or for getCacheStatusByCredentialIds grouping

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `deleteCache` tRPC mutation and a `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` repository method, but it does not include any test changes. However, the proposed finding is about missing tests (coverage), not a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. Also, the diff alone cannot prove there are no existing tests elsewhere in the repo covering these paths. Therefore this is not a verifiable problem in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/package.json: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx as a devDependency, so the script depends on a runtime network fetch and an unpinned version

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows the script change from `ts-node` to `npx tsx` and does not include (or show) the `dependencies`/`devDependencies` sections of `apps/web/package.json`. Therefore it is not verifiable from this diff whether `tsx` is missing as a devDependency. Also, `npx tsx` will use a locally installed `tsx` if present, so the claim that it necessarily causes a runtime network fetch/unpinned version is not provable from the diff alone.
